scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

Here’s why it matters so much: ### ✨ **Why This Ritual Works for You:** - **Psychological Anchoring:** Taking time to blend foundation or perfect eyeliner isn’t "wasted time"— it’s a mindful practice that signals to your brain: * "I am worthy of care before I face the world."* This builds confidence *before* the day even starts. - **Control & Predictability:** In a chaotic world, a consistent routine like this gives you a sense of agency. You’re creating a small, beautiful ritual *you* control—no external demands, just *your* hands, *your* choices, *your* time. - **The "Put-Together" Feeling is Real:** Neuroscience backs this up! When we intentionally care for our appearance (even just for ourselves), it triggers dopamine release and reduces anxiety. It’s not about others’ perception; it’s about *your* internal state. You’re literally *rewiring* your mindset to feel capable and centered. - **It’s Self-Respect in Action:** Society often dismisses " vanity," but this is deeper than that. It’s a daily reminder that * you* matter. You’re not just " getting ready for the day"— you’re *preparing yourself* for the day. That’s powerful. ### 💡 **A gentle reminder (if you ever need it):** - **Your time is sacred.** 15 minutes of intentional self-care is an investment in your mental well-being—not a luxury. - **" put-together" doesn’t mean " perfect."** It means * you* feel aligned, calm, and ready. That’s all that matters. - **If anyone ever judges it:** You’re allowed to say, " This is my way of showing up as my best self. It’s non negotiable for my mental health." (And they’d be wrong to question it.) ### 🌟 **Final Thought:** Keep doing this. Whether it’s 5 minutes or 30, *your* ritual is a form of self-love that radiates outward. The fact that you *notice* how it makes you feel is proof it’s working. That’s not " trivial"— it’s **profoundly human.** (And if you ever want to share your favorite product or step in the process?
